title: Iconography
summary: Icons are a compact visual language; ambiguity and missing accessible names cause failures.

MUST.text: Use one coherent icon family with consistent size, stroke and corner radius.
Provide an accessible name (aria-label/aria-labelledby or visually hidden text) for every icon-only control.
Use icons at standard sizes (16, 20, 24px) and align to text baseline; keep touch targets >=44x44px (see RSP-005).

SHOULD.text: Pair unfamiliar or high-impact actions with visible text.
Use filled variants for selected/active states and outline for default when the family supports it.
Test icon meaning with target users for non-universal metaphors.

AVOID.text: Emoji as product icons or obscure, invented metaphors.
Icon-only controls for destructive or irreversible actions.
Mixing multiple icon families or stroke weights.

DECIDE.decision: Icon + label on first use; icon-only after learning

EXAMPLE.good: "'Archive project' with archive icon + text, or icon-only with aria-label 'Archive project'."
EXAMPLE.bad: "Unlabeled box icon with no tooltip or accessible name."

FAILURE_MODES: Ambiguous icons cause misinterpretation and errors.
Missing accessible names block screen reader users.
Mixed families reduce perceived quality and consistency.
Small touch targets cause mis-taps on mobile.
